code: library(fmri.pipeline)  # One participant. All runs share the acquisition TR and voxel grid. # BOLD matrices: time x voxel, retaining all acquisition rows. # Each matrix needs identical unique voxel column names, in identical order. bold <- list(runA = bold_A, runB = bold_B, runC = bold_C) events <- list(runA = events_A, runB = events_B, runC = events_C) # Each event table: onset (seconds), condition (e.g., cue/response/feedback), # optional duration (seconds, zero for impulses). # First acquisition is time zero unless time_offset is supplied. parcel_ids <- setNames(parcel_for_each_voxel, colnames(bold$runA)) candidates <- hrf_library(tr = TR)  fit <- estimate_crossrun_hrf(   bold, events, tr = TR, kernel_grid = candidates,   spatial_groups = parcel_ids, pooling = "parcel",   nuisance = nuisance_by_run, valid_rows = usable_by_run,   time_offset = first_acquisition_time_by_run,   return_scores = TRUE )  # This is an alternative fit, not another smoothing pass on the parcel fit. voxel_fit <- estimate_crossrun_hrf(   bold, events, tr = TR, kernel_grid = candidates,   spatial_groups = parcel_ids, pooling = "voxel", spatial_strength = 0.02,   amplitude_model = "trial",   nuisance = nuisance_by_run, valid_rows = usable_by_run,   time_offset = first_acquisition_time_by_run )  # Example lambda and strength are not recommendations for every dataset. # Choose externally or within training data, without target-run RPE optimization. result <- deconvolve_crossrun_hrf(   bold, fit, lambda = 0.01, scaling = "zscore", backend = "cpp",   batch_size = 2048, operator_cache_mb = 128 ) saveRDS(result, "crossrun_hrf_deconvolution.rds") activity_A <- result$activity$runA fit$training_runs$runA      # runB, runC fit$selections$runA         # which HRF was applied, evidence, and fallback status fit$parcels$runA            # training-derived parcel anchors and support

code: 1. Compute the residuals of the model at each voxel at the group level. 2. Generate a null distribution by randomizing among subjects the signs of the residuals in the test (and permuting subject data sets between groups, if doing a two-sample test without covariates),    repeat the t-tests (with covariates, if present), and iterate 10,000 times. 3. Level 3 (Group): Mixed-effects (FLAME 1/2) combination across subjects. additional level, session wave, introduced, researchers must decide fold extra temporal dimension FSL’s rigid 3-level structure. FSL generally struggles true repeated-measures modeling, observations non-independent due within-subject clustering. mitigate , fmri.pipeline offers workarounds.

title: Analysis of fMRI Data on HPC clusters
text: Longitudinal fMRI analyses require special care runs, sessions, subjects represent distinct sources variation. current recommended patterns : Use l2_scope = "id_session" longitudinal studies. creates one Level 2 output per subject-session. Use l3_input_mode = "pooled_sessions_subject_ev" balanced categorical visit comparisons remain inside FSL. Use l3_input_mode = "3dlmer" irregular visits, incomplete follow-, continuous time effects, treatment--time interactions, random-effects structures better handled AFNI 3dLMEr. Reserve l2_scope = "id" cases sessions essentially pseudo-runs longitudinal change target. repository includes worked face/house demonstration longitudinal_fmri_demo_jun2026/, including walkthrough script YAML model file.

title: R6 class for 3dClustSim automation — afni_3dclustsim
text: out_dir intended output directory 3dClustSim files prefix prefix included names 3dClustSim output files fwhmx_input_files character vector input files passed 3dFWHMx (-ACF method) fwhmx_mask_files character vector masks containing volume estimate ACF 3dFWHMx. Must match 1:1 fwhmx_input_files. residuals_file filename group residuals file used null dataset generation (permutation approach). residuals_mask_file volume null datasets generated residuals residuals_njobs number independent jobs splitting residuals permutations. NULL, 32 jobs used. inset_files character vector dataset files pass directly 3dClustSim via -inset. insdat_file sdat file containing null datasets passed 3dClustSim via -insdat. insdat_mask_file mask file corresponding insdat_file maps values space. dxyz size voxels x y z (vector 3 numbers) nxyz number voxels along x y z (vector 3 positive integers) clustsim_mask controls volume correct FWE using 3dClustSim. give whole-brain mask, cluster thresholds reflect whole-brain FWE correction. give smaller mask (e.g., single region network), correcting volume (.e., small-volume correction). acf_params vector 3 autocorrelation parameters (, b, c) used simulate smoothness. Usually produced 3dFWHMx. '' parameter must 0 1. 'b' 'c' parameters (scale radii) must positive. spatial autocorrelation function given : `ACF(r) = * exp(-r*r/(2*b*b)) + (1-)*exp(-r/c)` nopad TRUE, disable 3dClustSim's default 'padding' slices along face allow edge effects smoothing process. Default: FALSE pthr vector voxelwise p-values tested 3dClustSim (-pthr). Can space-separated string numeric vector. Default: ".01 .005 .002 .001 .0005 .0002 .0001". athr vector cluster p-values tested 3dClustSim (-athr). Can space-separated string numeric vector. Default: ".05 .02 .01 .005 .002 .001 .0005 .0002 .0001". iter number iterations use simulating null datasets 3dClustSim. Default: 30000. nodec TRUE, clusters printed without decimal places, rounding (e.g., 27.2 becomes 28). Default: FALSE. seed seed use starting 3dClustSim random number generation. Default: 0 (sets random seed) scheduler HPC scheduler use. Can 'local', 'slurm', 'torque'. ncpus number cores use 3dClustSim job. sets OMP_NUM_THREADS 3dClustSim job speed computation.

title: Creates an fmri design matrix, including timing files for for AFNI or FSL. — build_design_matrix
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{   data(example_events)   data(example_signals)    #basic convolved design matrix   d <- build_design_matrix(     events = example_events,     signals = example_signals,     tr = 1.0,     plot = FALSE   )    data(example_nuisrun1) #load demo additional signals   data(example_nuisrun2)    #design matrix with 0,1,2 polynomial baseline regressors and a set of additional regressors   #this does not contain a 'taskness' regressor for cue or outcome   dnuis <- build_design_matrix(     events = example_events,     signals = example_signals,     tr = 1.0,     additional_regressors = list(example_nuisrun1, example_nuisrun2),     baseline_coef_order = 2   )    #tweak the design to add temporal derivatives for both ev and pe   example_signals$pe$add_deriv <- TRUE   example_signals$ev$add_deriv <- TRUE    #also use the evtmax_1 normalization method for both parametric signals   example_signals$pe$normalization <- "evtmax_1"   example_signals$ev$normalization <- "durmax_1"    #finally, add a taskness regressor for cue and outcome   example_signals$cue_evt <- list(value=1, event="cue", normalization="none")   example_signals$outcome_evt <- list(value=1, event="outcome", normalization="none")    #include up to quadratic drift terms in the design, drop 3 volumes from the beginning,   #and write timing files in AFNI, FSL, and convolved formats (to the "run_timing" directory).   d_modified <- build_design_matrix(     events = example_events,     signals = example_signals,     tr = 1.0,     baseline_coef_order = 2,     drop_volumes = 3,     write_timing_files = c("convolved", "AFNI", "FSL")   )    #show unconvolved design   plot(visualize_design_matrix(concat_design_runs(d_modified, convolved=FALSE)))    #beta series approach for cues: 1 regressor per cue event   example_signals$cue_evt$beta_series <- TRUE   example_signals$ev <- NULL   example_signals$pe <- NULL    d_beta <- build_design_matrix(     events = example_events,     signals = example_signals,     tr = 1.0,     plot = FALSE,     baseline_coef_order = 2,     drop_volumes = 3,     write_timing_files = c("convolved", "FSL")   )    #PPI example    events <- rbind(     data.frame(event="cue", run_number=1, trial=1:5, onset=c(5, 20, 50, 100, 150), duration=4),     data.frame(event="cue", run_number=2, trial=1:5, onset=c(15, 35, 60, 90, 105), duration=4)   )    signals <- list(     load=list(value=rbind(       data.frame(run_number=1, trial=1:5, value=1:5),       data.frame(run_number=2, trial=1:5, value=1:5)     ), event="cue", normalization="none"),     cue_evt=list(value=1, event="cue", normalization="none"),     cue_evt_ppi=list(value=1, event="cue", normalization="none", ts_multipliers="vs")   )    library(neuRosim)   forppi1 <- simTSrestingstate(nscan=328, base=1, TR=1, SNR=6)   forppi2 <- simTSrestingstate(nscan=242, base=1, TR=1, SNR=6)   test_ppi <- list(run1=data.frame(vs=forppi1), run2=data.frame(vs=forppi2))    #In PPI, the time series itself should typically be included as a regressor   d <- build_design_matrix(events = events, signals = signals, tr=0.5, center_values=TRUE,                 write_timing_files = c("convolved", "AFNI", "FSL"),                 drop_volumes = 0, baseline_coef_order = 2, run_volumes = c(328, 242),                 ts_multipliers = test_ppi, additional_regressors = test_ppi) } # }

text: n_vols number volumes (scans) output convolved regressor onsets vector times (volumes seconds) specifying event onsets durations vector durations (volumes seconds) event values vector parametric values used regressor heights prior convolution units Specifies units measurement `onsets` `durations`. `"seconds"`, interpreted terms time seconds. `"volumes"`, onsets durations interpreted terms volumes scan. Thus, onset `1` volumes refers time = 0s, extension, `time = (volume - 1)*tr`. Default: `"seconds"`. center_values Whether demean values vector convolution rm_zeros Whether remove zeros events vector prior convolution. Generally good idea since typically center values prior convolution, retaining zeros lead non-zero mean centering. convolve Whether convolve regressor HRF. FALSE, time series events, durations, heights returned. tr repetition time (sometimes called TR) seconds ts_multiplier time series length n_vols multiplied stimulus convolution. demean Whether demean regressor convolution. Default: TRUE convmax_1 Whether rescale convolved regressor maximum height 1. a1 a1 parameter double gamma a2 a2 parameter double gamma b1 b1 parameter double gamma b2 b2 parameter double gamma cc cc parameter double gamma conv_method Method convolving HRF stimulus. Either "r" "cpp". "r" method uses FFT-based internal convolution convolve(x, y, conj=TRUE). "cpp" method uses internal C++ function loop-based convolution vectors. Unfortunately, present, C++ approach noticeably slower since use FFT obtain filter. microtime_resolution number bins TRs used calculating regressor values continuous time

text: element regressors list list specifying handle given regressor. Required elements list : Optional elements list :
code: $waveform: The type of input for this regressor. Options are:      "custom_1"    : 1-column text file containing regressor values (can be convolved or unconvolved)      "custom_3"    : 3-column FSL-format text file containing onset time, duration, and regressor value      "empty"       : an all-zero regressor      "square"      : for block design (not currently supported)      "sinusoid"    : for periodic regressors (not currently supported)      "interaction" : unclear what this is, but exists in .fsf files (not currently supported)    $convolution: The type of convolution function to be applied to the $waveform. Options are:      "none"         : no convolution is applied (esp. useful when using custom_1 files that are already convolved)      "double_gamma" : convolve with FSL-variant of double gamma function      "gaussian"     : convolve with Gaussian function (not tested)      "gamma_basis"  : Gamma basis functions (not tested)      "sine_basis"   : sine basis functions (not tested)      "fir_basis"    : finite impulse response (FIR) basis functions (not tested)      "alternate_double_gamma" : what it sounds like (not tested)    $name: The name of the EV (i.e., regressor) in the model specification and output. $timing_file: the name of the text file containing regressor values. Used by "custom_1" and "custom_3".   $tempfilt: whether to apply temporal filtering to the regressor, as with the fMRI data. Default: 1 (TRUE)   $deriv: whether to add a temporal derivative for this regressor to the model. Default 0 (FALSE)   $convolve_phase: not entirely sure what it does but is 0/1. Default: 0 (FALSE)

text: bdm object (class 'bdm') generated build_design_matrix. particular, function uses $design $run_niftis elements extract relevant regressors information NIfTI files analyze. ts_files character vector nuisance text files – one per run – added covariates SPM's multi_reg field. output_dir path SPM scripts outputs go design matrix. path can relative absolute, converted absolute internally using normalizePath(). hpf high-pass filter cutoff (seconds) used remove low frequencies prior analysis. Default: 100 hrf_derivs Whether include derivatives regressors model capture HRF variation. Options : "none", "time" (temporal derivative), "time_dispersion" (temporal dispersion derivatives). Default: "none" cvi Serial correlations model. Options : "AR(1)", "FAST", "none". Default: "AR(1)" estimation_method Estimation method. Options : "Classical" "Bayesian2". Default: "Classical" write_residuals Whether write residual images. supported Classical estimation. Default: FALSE fmri_t Microtime resolution (number time bins per scan). Default: 20 fmri_t0 Microtime onset (reference bin). Default: 1 nifti_tmpdir place uncompressed NIfTIs analysis (SPM handle .nii.gz) cleanup_tmp Whether remove uncompressed .nii files completing function condition_contrasts Whether setup contrasts condition. multi-run data, contrasts represent condition average across runs (e.g., [ .5, .5 ] 2 runs). Default: TRUE unit_contrasts Whether estimate unit-height contrast every regressor design. essentially includes diagonal matrix contrast specification. Default: FALSE effects_of_interest_F Whether include single F test contrast regressors interest. Useful adjusting VOIs nuisance regressors. Default: TRUE spm_execute_setup Whether run GLM setup script MATLAB, creating SPM.mat. Default: FALSE spm_execute_glm Whether run GLM creating SPM.mat. take ! Default: FALSE spm_execute_contrasts Whether compute contrasts GLM complete. Depends spm_execute_glm. Default: FALSE concatenate_runs Whether convert multi-run data single concatenated session. execute spm_fmri_concatenate GLM setup complete. script computes run-specific whitening high-pass filters keeping single concatenated time series. useful preamble DCM, often uses concatenated time series. Default: FALSE spm_path path spm12 directory. included MATLAB scripts ensure spm found. matlab_cmd Command launch MATLAB/Octave. Default: "matlab" matlab_args Arguments passed MATLAB/Octave. Default: "-batch" compute_env Optional character vector shell commands prepare environment (e.g., module load statements). prepended direct MATLAB execution.

AR/calibrated fits use observation masks scaling fitting default. Nuisance adjustment remains explicit; optional joint projection applies convolution observations. what: Cross-run HRF estimation and spatial regularization
title: fmri.pipeline 0.4-1
text: hrf_library() constructs small unit-sum HRF library. estimate_crossrun_hrf() selects HRFs using runs , batched Rcpp/BLAS training fits, nuisance regressors, observation masks, explicit support gates, recorded parcel/prespecified fallback hierarchy. Training can use condition means free event amplitudes signed trial responses otherwise average away, without supplying RPE values. Explicit parcel pooling optional voxel shape penalties toward training-derived parcel HRFs provide spatial regularization. constrain HRF selection without spatially smoothing recovered neural activity. Strength effect-size thresholds user-controlled. original heuristic mode supply significance tests. deconvolve_crossrun_hrf() applies frozen HRFs required fixed lambda, grouped inverse operators, bounded caching, block multiplication, recorded per-voxel scaling. Existing NIfTI/file deconvolution defaults unchanged. See CROSSRUN_HRF_GUIDE.md reproducible review/benchmark scripts. HRF_ESTIMATION_VALIDATION.md reports 480 independent simulated datasets comparing learned, canonical, true HRFs three fixed inverse penalties. Learning helps stable shape mismatch can hurt low SNR, zero-mean signed responses, run changes, neural-duration mismatch. original support gate accepted null free-event fits colored noise; support labels confidence measures. Estimator settings tuned results. Reproducible scripts, compact tables, figures included.

what: Auditable event overlap and impulse recovery
title: fmri.pipeline 0.4-1

what: Bug fixes in build_design_matrix / fmri.stimulus convolution
title: fmri.pipeline 0.4-1
text: Fix: overlapping events silently overwritten stimulus construction. construct_stimulus (inside fmri.stimulus) used assignment (stim[idx] <- values[]) building microtime stimulus vector. two events overlapped time (e.g., long-duration events short ITIs), later events overwrote earlier ones, silently producing incorrect regressors. Fixed use additive accumulation (stim[idx] <- stim[idx] + values[]), correct linearity convolution. affected normalization modes (none, durmax_1, evtmax_1). Fix: microtime bin truncation causing position-dependent convolution peaks. Floating-point arithmetic fmri.stimulus converting onset times microtime bins produce values like 2013.999... instead 2014, R truncated wrong bin. shifted events one microtime step, causing identical events different run positions ~0.4% different peak amplitudes. Fixed applying round() microtime onset duration indices. Optimized evtmax_1 normalization. Replaced previous approach N separate full-run FFT convolutions (one per event) precomputed HRF peaks via small padded windows, followed single combined convolution. also eliminates previous fragile workaround end--run events (re-convolving center run estimate “true” peak). Speedups 2-9x depending number events, number unique durations, run length. Thread microtime_resolution parameter convolve_regressor ensure peak lookups grid-phase computation always use resolution main convolution. Fix: insufficient convolution padding sub-second TRs. convolve_stimulus used fixed 20-TR padding edge-effect suppression, TR=0.5s 10 seconds — enough double-gamma HRF undershoot decay (still ~-0.02 20s). Changed 30 seconds absolute time padding regardless TR, preventing circular convolution artifacts near run boundaries multiband acquisitions.
